purpose: The card token vault tokenizes primary account numbers (PANs) for the payment services and is the only component that stores them. All other services handle tokens.

components.name: vault-db
components.evidence: vault-db (PostgreSQL): encrypted card records and the token mapping.

components.name: Vault and KMS
components.evidence: Vault and KMS: data encryption keys and runtime secrets.

components.name: vault private subnet
components.evidence: vault private subnet: the network around the vault.

flows.evidence: Calls from payment services to the tokenization-service are authenticated with mutual TLS or signed workload identity tokens.
The tokenization-service writes a log line for every tokenize and detokenize call.
the tokenizer (that's tokenization-service, I always say tokenizer) gets a PAN, asks Vault and KMS for a data key, encrypts, stores, hands back a token.
The database sits in private subnets with no public endpoint.
